https://www.touchstonemag.com/archives/a.text: ART BOOK A Thousand Words: Reflections On Art and Christianity A Touchstone Reader Creed & Culture II View The Chapel at the End of the Earth Andrei Romanov on Christian Europe’s First & Last Resort T he first structure Henry the Navigator (1394–1460) built at Sagres, Portugal, was a chapel, an intentional act that foreshadowed the spiritual and ideological priorities that guided his subsequent undertakings. Not a harbor. Not a watchtower. Not the legendary school of navigation that may or may not have existed; historians still fight about that. Before the maps, before the caravels, before the first shaking crew rounded Cape Bojador into waters that European sailors believed were boiling and full of sea monsters, Prince Henry built a small stone church at the edge of a cliff overlooking the Atlantic and dedicated it to Our Lady of Grace. I know this because I live twelve minutes from the church and surrounding fortress. As a Romanian historian who moved to the Algarve to research a book about the Portuguese Age of Discovery, I have stood inside that chapel, the Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Graça, more times than I can count. The familiarity of this place has shaped my understanding of why Henry built the chapel first, before any other structure, as an acknowledgment of the spiritual foundation beneath the era’s ambitions. https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2.text: France’s high school students will stage new protests on Tuesday, the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency is reporting, A government source told journalists last week that the cost for damage caused by the demonstrations, which have shaken an unpopular government trying to reduce a ballooning budget deficit, was already “at least 30 million euros”. Widespread disillusionment has seen young people protest over recent weeks against what they say is underfunding and neglect of the education system, with the demonstrations marred by often violent clashes that have injured hundreds. Trying to appease the student’s demands, the government announced last week that about 3,000 substitute teachers would be deployed in the coming days to replace absent staff at the 114 worst-affected high schools. https://www.dw.com/en/flavio-bolsonaro-l.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Omfr News of Bolsonaro departing Brazil broke on Tuesday, just two days after Brazil's presidential elections Image: Ricardo Arduengo/AFP Advertisement Brazilian right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami, Florida in the US on Wednesday morning. His plan to leave Brazil became public knowledge late on Tuesday , soon after he had refused to concede defeat in Sunday's presidential elections and pledged to challenge the results. Bolsonaro refused to comply with a Brazilian Supreme Court order to surrender his passports, tied to a money-laundering investigation in which he denies wrongdoing, and the US State Department later said it would grant him and his family visas. The Bolsonaro's were escorted to a vehicle under cover of umbrellas Image: Eva Marie Uzcategui/REUTERS When did Bolsonaro arrive, how did he reach Miami? Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters were seen disembarking a Gulfstream G400 plane and heading into the Miami-Opa Locka airport on Wednesday morning. Their journey across the Americas had captured regional attention. The quartet first flew into Argentina late on Tuesday, then took a private jet to the Ecuadorean city of Guayaquil. From there, they continued to Miami in Florida. As a sitting senator Bolsonaro had immunity from prosecution but he had announced plans to give up that role to challenge Lula for the presidency Image: Ricardo Arduengo/AFP Bolsonaro would lose his immunity from prosecution in February when his term in the Senate ends. On Monday, he had said in an Instagram post that he had no intention of leaving the country and that he would "hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me." According to the AFP news agency, Bolsonaro also holds Italian citizenship and so was able to travel despite his Brazilian and diplomatic passports being canceled. Bolsonaro's flights out of Brazil and towards Miami had been tracked overnight Image: Eva Marie Uzcategui/REUTERS Potential source of strain between Trump's US and Lula's Brazil Bolsonaro's departure and his arrival in Florida — like his father Jair Bolsonaro before him after Brazil's previous presidential elections — could deepen a rift between the two most populous countries in the Americas. During the election campaign, incumbent Luiz Inacio "Lula" da Silva had accused the Donald Trump administration of colluding with the Bolsonaro family in a bid to help them return to power. After the election results, Trump appeared to question the integrity of the vote, saying he thought the extension to voting times was a "very bad look." He had also alleged in the past that Jair Bolsonaro was the victim of judicial persecution in Brazil. Bolsonaro senior is now in jail in Brazil on charges of leading a conspiracy designed to keep him in power despite defeat in 2022's presidential election. https://pt.euronews.com/2026/10/16/uniao.text: Os líderes da União Europeia entraram em conflito sobre a migração irregular na fase final de uma cimeira de dois dias em Bruxelas, prolongando as discussões para além da hora prevista para o fim.A Dinamarca, a Polónia e a Itália pressionaram para que fossem introduzidas alterações às conclusões, incluindo uma referência indireta ao plano de regularização em grande escala da Espanha, que abrange 600 000 migrantes indocumentados.Um novo projeto de trabalho obtido pela Euronews instava os países a evitar "medidas que pudessem criar incentivos à migração ilegal".O projeto apelava também à Comissão Europeia para que reforçasse a coordenação das políticas nacionais de migração que pudessem afetar outros Estados-Membros, outra exigência apresentada em conjunto pelo trio, que é vista como uma repreensão ao governo de esquerda de Madrid.Na sexta-feira, o presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskyy solicitou aos líderes da UE que concedessem 70 mil milhões de euros em apoio financeiro e militar adicional no próximo ano, um montante avultado que provavelmente irá abalar o bloco num momento de aumento da dívida e dos custos de financiamento.Zelenskyy afirmou ainda que o seu país «se manterá firme» enquanto o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, celebra acordos com o seu homólogo russo, Vladimir Putin, e compromete a frente comum da aliança transatlântica."Defendo exclusivamente os interesses da Ucrânia e do povo ucraniano. Fomos atacados, ocupados e o nosso povo foi morto. É lógico que tenhamos o direito de nos defendermos", afirmou Zelenskyy na sua conferência de imprensa, respondendo a uma pergunta da Euronews. "E por muito que a Rússia queira restringir todos os nossos direitos, é claro que temos o direito de nos defendermos."As suas declarações surgem num momento em que Trump intensifica o confronto, classificando a estratégia de Kiev de atacar refinarias de petróleo russas como uma «vergonha» e exigindo novas eleições no país."Considero que é mais difícil lidar com Zelenskyy do que com Putin", afirmou Trump à Newsmax.Acompanhe as atualizações no nosso liveblog em inglês.

Bucharest: All nine Indian seafarers on board chemical tanker YARA J are safe, and the vessel has arrived at the Port of Constanta in Romania, the Embassy of India in Bucharest said Saturday. The confirmation came after India’s Ambassador to Romania, Manoj Mohapatra, spoke with Romanian authorities and the Company Security Officer (CSO) of the tanker. “Amb. Manoj Mohapatra spoke with Romanian authorities, including SAR Romania and MRCC Constanta, as well as the CSO of the chemical tanker YARA J (IMO: 9221803). It was confirmed that all nine Indian seafarers on board are safe and the vessel has arrived at the Port of Constanta. The Ambassador assured them of the Government of India’s full support and assistance,” the Embassy posted on X.

Last week, three Indian nationals rescued from the commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov, which came under attack in the Black Sea, departed from Romania for India, the Embassy had said. “Three Indian nationals, Shri Sahil Sandhu, Shri Ashwini Kumar and Shri Harman Singh, departed for India today. The Embassy provided all necessary support and assistance to facilitate their return,” Embassy had posted on X. “We express our sincere gratitude to the Romanian authorities, Constanta County Hospital, and the Romanian rescue teams for their invaluable assistance, cooperation and support,” it added. The three Indians were rescued from the vessel October 6. On October 7, India condemned attacks targeting commercial vessels in the Black Sea region and reiterated its call for dialogue and diplomacy to de-escalate tensions and enable an early return of peace in the region. Addressing a bi-weekly media briefing in New Delhi, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that attacks targeting commercial vessels threaten commercial shipping and endanger the lives of the seafaring community. “We have seen a string of attacks targeting commercial vessels in the Black Sea region in the last one or two days. We condemn such attacks that threaten commercial shipping and endanger lives of our seafaring community. First, the commercial vessel MV Royad Mammadov came under attack while it was flying in the Black Sea. There were three Indian nationals onboard. All of them are safe, but one of them got injured, and he is receiving treatment. We thank the Romanian authorities who lent us a helping hand and have been very helpful in this particular incident,” Jaiswal added.

Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, and his wife, Lori Huang, with Apple's Tim Cook at the top table during a state dinner hosted by Donald Trump for Xi Jinping at the White House in September. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images US news Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing Marina Dunbar and Robert Mackey Sun 8 Nov 2026 19.25 EST First published on Sun 8 Nov 2026 16.00 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”. The New York Times reported in ​October that Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence that Huang ‌had a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump downplayed the revelations about Huang, who is an influential adviser to the president on artificial intelligence, saying: “I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it.” Trump also brushed off a question about whether he now regrets not acting on the intelligence when he was briefed on it, and suggested that he would be happy to take Huang with him on a trip to Asia next week. “I haven’t heard he’s done anything wrong,” Trump said. “He dealt with somebody. But, you know, so does everybody else.” Republican lawmakers have expressed more alarm, asking Huang to give the House foreign affairs and intelligence committees a closed-door briefing next week on Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” and his relationship with Alice Huang or Huang Le, an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed, who is of no relation to the Nvidia CEO. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her. Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources. The company’s board said in a statement on Sunday that, while it has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information. “The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.” Huang fully ‌supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added. Axios reported on ​Sunday, citing a draft email by Huang to employees, that Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full ⁠responsibility for his actions. “I was unfaithful to my ​wife. My ​actions hurt her ​and our children. There is no excuse ​for what ‌I did,” ​Huang said ​in the draft email also seen by Reuters. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Axios report. The Times reported on Sunday that a memo drafted by US secretary of state Marco Rubio circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring, citing intelligence that the businesswoman who had a relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive was a spy for China’s ministry of state security. Despite those concerns, Huang was invited to join Trump’s delegation when he traveled to China in May. Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, were also invited to a state dinner at the White House in September for Xi Jinping and seated at the top table with Trump and China’s president. Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom, placing Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development. Tech sell-off drives US markets down by nearly $1tn after subpar earnings reports Read more However, national security concerns have prompted strict US export controls, effectively barring the company from selling its top-tier processors to customers in China. US officials have cited threats to the US supply chain and fears over national security risks as a rationale for the restrictions. Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, has also suggested that China could be sanctioned for theft of US data and intellectual property. The Trump administration has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips to China as a matter of national security. Megaspeed’s Alice Huang was suspected to have been helping the government get around those restrictions. The investigation also follows a rough few days on Wall Street for AI tech firms, particularly Nvidia. A sell-off of tech stocks that began earlier this month and gained steam with disappointing earnings led to a total decline of nearly $1tn in value off the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange in one week and erased about $2tn in a month. A drop of 3.1% for Nvidia, previously worth about $5tn, whose chips have made it the poster child of the AI frenzy, was the heaviest force pulling the S&P 500 downward recently.
